corrections.text: The article quotes Hashimoto directly as saying multiplexers 'duplicate everything the user types and have to constantly reconcile local and remote states' and that 'even slapping a modern terminal such as Kitty, Alacritty or Ghostty in front of a multiplexer won't do much to speed ops.' In The Register's original reporting, these sentences carry no quotation marks — they are the reporter's own paraphrase of what Hashimoto 'explained... in a video posted on X,' not verbatim quotes attributed to him. Separately, the quote 'It does require that every connecting client be a very smart, high-functioning, compliant client' is genuine and correctly attributed to Hashimoto, but the article's quotation marks were extended to also cover 'such as one built on libghostty,' which in the source is the reporter's own added clarification, not part of what Hashimoto said.

The article attributes the quotes 'exactly as it was designed to be used: as a public building block for terminal applications,' 'upstream shared terminal work so every libghostty consumer can benefit,' and 'remains a non-profit; its mission, governance, license, technical goals, and roadmap do not change' to 'Superlogical says... on its site.' These are verbatim, but they actually appear in Mitchell Hashimoto's first-person personal essay at mitchellh.com/writing/superlogical, not on the superlogical.com company site as the sentence implies.
